newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX retreats on dollar, Dow weakness.
newsitem.headline: German DAX retreats on dollar, Dow weakness.

text.p: German shares on Tuesday reversed most of the gains made the previous day, with dealers saying the overnight retreat of the dollar and weakness on Wall Street were dampening sentiment.
"We have lost what we gained yesterday, but volumes are relatively weak. Most players have had enough and just want to celebrate Christmas," said one dealer.
The DAX-30 index of 30 top German shares fell 34.80 points, or 1.22 percent, to 2,820.99 in the first half an hour of trade, wiping out most of the 56-point gain made on Monday.

The dollar had on Monday firmed on the perception that the monetary union stability pact reached by European finance ministers in Dublin on Friday made Europe's planned currency union all the more likely, thus reducing the power of the mark.

But overnight the U.S. currency slipped more than 1/2 pfennig to around 1.545 marks on worries ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, although most analysts expected no change in U.S. interest rates.
The dollar's weakness weighed particularly on export-oriented stocks such as chemicals companies BASF AG and Bayer AG.
But dealers said trading was pretty thin, with players keen to close positions ahead of the year-end.
German software major SAP AG registered the only other significant movement, slipping 3.60 marks to 208.50 on the weakness of U.S. technology stocks overnight.
